question: The deflection sensitivity (s) of a CRT (cathode ray tube) is defined as: (where D is deflection of the screen and E is defection voltage)
solution:
The correct answer is __s = D/E**(Deflection Sensitivity)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Deflection Sensitivity__ is abbreviated as 's'.
 
• Deflection sensitivity (s) is a measure of the displacement of the beam per unit deflection voltage.
 
• The formula is expressed as s = D/E, where:
 __
 
• D is the deflection of the beam on the CRT screen.
 
• E is the deflection voltage applied to the plates.
 
 
• A higher sensitivity means greater deflection per unit voltage.
 
• The deflection sensitivity is a key parameter for understanding the performance of CRTs in oscilloscopes and other display devices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **CRT (Cathode Ray Tube):**
 
 
• A CRT is an electronic display device that uses electron beams to produce images.
 
• It consists of a cathode, anode, deflection plates, and a phosphorescent screen.
 
 
 
• **Applications of CRT: **
 
 
• Used in oscilloscopes for measuring voltages.
 
• Used in older television and computer monitors for displaying images.
 
 
 
• **Deflection Plates:**
 
 
• Horizontal and vertical plates are used to deflect the electron beam.
 
• The applied voltage to these plates controls the beam's position on the screen.
